BE AS DETAILED AS POSSIBLE!!! The AGE Flight and Propulsion Flight is seeking a movable liquid CO2 (LCO2) horizontal ISO tank capable of supporting a Dry Ice Production Hub manufactured by Cold Jet. The tank shall be transportable/movable and suitable for relocation as operational requirements dictate. The tank should have a capacity of 19,000-21,000 liters and be a vacuum-insulated double wall tank consisting of two vessels, a low-temperature resistant austenitic steel inner tank and an outer tank made of steel with an anti-corrosion primer and a top coat of paint. The tank should be ﬁlled to 90% of the capacity of the tank with LCO2 and ready for operation after contract completion. The maximum allowable working pressure for the inner vessel must be 22 bar gauge for temperatures ranging from -196° up to 20°C. It must supply pressurized LCO2 at 189-261 psi (13-18 bar), with an optimal operating range of 15-16 bar (-26°C

The classifications are listed in alphabetical order under rate identifiers indicating whether the particular rate is a union rate (current union negotiated rate), a survey rate, a weighted union average rate, a state adopted rate, or a supplemental classification rate. Union Rate Identifiers A four-letter identifier beginning with characters other than � SU � , � UAVG � , � SA � , or � SC � denotes that a union rate was prevailing for that classification in the survey. Example: PLUM0198-005 07/01/2024. PLUM is an identifier of the union whose collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers. 0198 indicates the local union number or district council number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated rate. Union prevailing wage rates are updated to reflect all changes over time that are reported to WHD in the rates in the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) governing the classification. Union Average Rate Identifiers The UAVG identifier indicates that no single rate prevailed for those classifications, but that 100% of the data reported for the classifications reflected union rates. PROJECT PROFILE Thi s scoping mission would identify, evaluate, and develop funding recommendations for up to six (6) initial and eight (8) full reviews of digital infrastructure project opportunities across the Europe and Eurasia (EE) region for USTDA funding consideration. Count ries across the EE region are rapidly investing in digital infrastructure projects, including cybersecurity, artificial intelligence (“AI”), data centers, and connectivity. Simultaneously, many EE countries have expressed their strong interest in diversifying their suppliers and working more closely with the United States. The EE Regional Team has received a number of proposals and expressions of interest that may be evaluated under this proposed DM. In particular, USTDA has received proposals for projects in Azerbaijan, Armenia, the Western Balkans, Moldova, and Uzbekistan, and proposals in other countries are anticipated as well. 21 Solicitation Number: 1131Pl26R0058 Solicitation Title: EUROPE AND EURASIA DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE

he EU’s “Digital Europe Program”, which supports projects in areas such as AI, advanced digital skills, and digital infrastructure, as well as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development’s (“EBRD”) “Go Digital in the Western Balkans” program. Relatedly, North Macedonia is implementing its National Operational Broadband Plan 2019–2029, which aims to expand its nationwide deployment of high-speed broadband and 5G infrastructure in line with Western connectivity standards. Additionally, Albania has announced plans to modernize its public administration through the use of AI, including in public procurement, taxation and customs, cybersecurity, and intelligence. Moreover, in 2025 Montenegro released its first “Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment” for public administration, which is intended to inform the country's first National AI Strategy currently in development. Similarly, Serbia adopted its “National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence for 2025-2030" which has a goal of advancing legislative frameworks and expanding AI applications in the public sector. The EE Regional Team has received inquiries from U.S. companies interested in the Western Balkans region and anticipates the submission of proposals for USTDA consideration.
